intent: Head a page or a section of one with its title, the controls and content around the title, and the actions the page is worked with.
typical_uses: The header of the page of one object - a customer, an order, a project, a document - with its name and a badge, a status or a link beside it
The header of a section inside a page, such as a list with its "New" button or a project tab with its own navigation and actions

dont_use_when.situation: The heading of a card or a panel that holds content
A trail of links to the pages above the current one, with no title of its own
A message about the state of the page, such as a failed request

invariants.text: The root renders a header element with no role of its own. Inside main, article, aside, nav or section - or an element with role main, article, complementary, navigation or region - it maps to no landmark; outside them it is a banner.
`border={false}` paints the bottom rule transparent rather than removing it, so the root's height and the position of its content are the same with and without the rule.

`size` sets the root's minimum height, the rule included - 56 for `sm`, 64 for `default`, 80 for `lg` - and the root grows past it when its content outgrows it, keeping var(--space-1) above and below its content.

When the root's width inside its side insets is below 64rem - read by a container query on the root rather than the viewport, so 64rem plus both insets outside them - the content beside the title moves under the description, the actions take a line of their own, the leading control stays on the first line beside the text, and each line keeps var(--space-2) above and below it, on top of the root's own var(--space-1).

anti_patterns.dont: Render the page header outside the page's main element as it is
anti_patterns.do_instead: Put it inside main, where its header element is no landmark; a header the layout keeps above main passes role="group", so it is not a second banner beside the application's top bar

anti_patterns.dont: Put a growing tab list or set of links straight into PageHeaderMeta
anti_patterns.do_instead: Wrap it in a block with overflow-x auto, so it scrolls rather than running under the actions, and leave room in that block for focus rings, which it clips vertically too

anti_patterns.dont: Remove the rule with a border style of your own
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `border={false}`, which keeps the rule's width inside the header, so the text sits exactly where it does with the rule; a border removed in CSS moves the text by half a rule and makes a header whose content outgrows the minimum height one rule shorter

anti_patterns.dont: Place the page header in a flex row without a width of its own
anti_patterns.do_instead: Give it `flex: 1` or a width there - its narrow layout measures the header, so it takes its width from its parent and collapses to its side insets when the parent sizes it to its content

good.title: A list's header with its title, a count and the button that adds to it
An object's page header above the page's main, in the tall size with the Page Title role

bad.title: The title and the actions put straight into the root
bad.why: The root is a row of three slots; without PageHeaderContent the title loses its grid area and its truncation width, and without PageHeaderActions the button gets neither the drawn 24 before it nor a line of its own in the narrow layout.
